text: At that time the monks from the group of six rubbed their bodies—thighs, arms, chest, and back—against walls while bathing. People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics do this? They’re just like boxers and city slickers who beautify their bodies!” …

original: “na, bhikkhave, nahāyamānena bhikkhunā kuṭṭe kāyo ugghaṁsetabbo. Yo ugghaṁseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t rub your body against a wall while bathing. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū aṭṭāne nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ …pe… “saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti …pe… vigarahitvā …pe… dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: At that time the monks from the group of six rubbed their bodies—thighs, arms, chest, and back—against a rubbing board while bathing. People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics do this? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “na, bhikkhave, aṭṭāne nahāyitabbaṁ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t rub your body against a rubbing board while bathing. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū gandhabbahatthakena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ …pe…
text: At that time the monks from the group of six bathed with a wooden rubbing-hand. People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics do this? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” The monks heard the complaints of those people and they told the Buddha.

original: “na, bhikkhave, gandhabbahatthakena nahāyitabbaṁ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t bathe with a wooden rubbing-hand. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kuruvindakasuttiyā nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six bathed with a string of cinnabar beads. People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics do this? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, kuruvindakasuttiyā nahāyitabbaṁ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t bathe with a string of cinnabar beads. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū viggayha parikammaṁ kārāpenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six massaged one another. People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics do this? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, viggayha parikammaṁ kārāpetabbaṁ. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t massage one another. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mallakena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six bathed with an ornamented scrubber. People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics do this? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” … They told the Buddha.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, mallakena nahāyitabbaṁ. Yo nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t bathe with an ornamented scrubber. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno kacchurogābādho hoti. Na tassa vinā mallakena phāsu hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards a certain monk had an itchy skin disease. He was not comfortable without a scrubber.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa akatamallakan”ti.
text: “I allow a plain scrubber for those who are sick.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu jarādubbalo nahāyamāno na sakkoti attano kāyaṁ ugghaṁsetuṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time a monk who was weak from old age was unable to rub his own body while bathing.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ukkāsikan”ti.
text: “I allow gloves of cloth.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū piṭṭhiparikammaṁ kātuṁ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Being afraid of wrongdoing, the monks did not give back massages.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puthupāṇikan”ti.
text: “I allow a massage with the flat of the hand.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vallikaṁ dhārenti …pe… pāmaṅgaṁ dhārenti …pe… kaṇṭhasuttakaṁ dhārenti …pe… kaṭisuttakaṁ dhārenti …pe… ovaṭṭikaṁ dhārenti …pe… kāyuraṁ dhārenti …pe… hatthābharaṇaṁ dhārenti …pe… aṅgulimuddikaṁ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six wore earrings, ornamental hanging strings, necklaces, ornamental girdles, bangles, armlets, bracelets, and rings. People complained and criticized them, “… They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” The monks heard the complaints of those people. They told the Buddha.
title: Personal beautification

original: “Saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vallikaṁ dhārenti …pe… pāmaṅgaṁ dhārenti, kaṇṭhasuttakaṁ dhārenti, kaṭisuttakaṁ dhārenti, ovaṭṭikaṁ dhārenti, kāyuraṁ dhārenti, hatthābharaṇaṁ dhārenti, aṅgulimuddikaṁ dhārentī”ti? “Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti …pe… vigarahitvā …pe… dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: “Is it true, monks, that the monks from the group of six are wearing these things?” “It’s true, sir.” … After rebuking them … the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

original: “na, bhikkhave, vallikā dhāretabbā …pe… na pāmaṅgo dhāretabbo … na kaṇṭhasuttakaṁ dhāretabbaṁ … na kaṭisuttakaṁ dhāretabbaṁ … na ovaṭṭikaṁ dhāretabbaṁ … na kāyuraṁ dhāretabbaṁ … na hatthābharaṇaṁ dhāretabbaṁ … na aṅgulimuddikā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t wear earrings, an ornamental hanging string, a necklace, an ornamental girdle, a bangle, an armlet, a bracelet, or a ring. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dīghe kese dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six grew their hair long. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, dīghā kesā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dumāsikaṁ vā duvaṅgulaṁ vā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t grow your hair long. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow you to grow it to a length of 3.5 centimeters or for two months at the most.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kocchena kese osaṇṭhenti …pe… phaṇakena kese osaṇṭhenti, hatthaphaṇakena kese osaṇṭhenti, sitthatelakena kese osaṇṭhenti, udakatelakena kese osaṇṭhenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six brushed their hair, and they combed it, combed it with their hands, smoothed it with beeswax, and smoothed it with water and oil. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, kocchena kesā osaṇṭhetabbā …pe… na sitthatelakena kesā osaṇṭhetabbā … na udakatelakena kesā osaṇṭhetabbā. Yo osaṇṭheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t brush your hair, or comb it, comb it with your hands, smooth it with beeswax, or smooth it with water and oil. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ādāsepi udakapattepi mukhanimittaṁ olokenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six looked at their faces in mirrors and in bowls of water. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, ādāse vā udakapatte vā mukhanimittaṁ oloketabbaṁ. Yo olokeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t look at your face in a mirror or in a bowl of water. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno mukhe vaṇo hoti. So bhikkhū pucchi— “kīdiso me, āvuso, vaṇo”ti? Bhikkhū evamāhaṁsu— “ediso te, āvuso vaṇo”ti. So na saddahati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards a certain monk had a sore on his face. He asked the monks, “What kind of sore is it?” They replied, “It’s this kind of sore.” He did not trust them.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā ādāse vā udakapatte vā mukhanimittaṁ oloketun”ti.
text: “I allow you to look at your face in a mirror or in a bowl of water if you have a disease.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mukhaṁ ālimpanti …pe… mukhaṁ ummaddenti, mukhaṁ cuṇṇenti, manosilikāya mukhaṁ lañchenti, aṅgarāgaṁ karonti, mukharāgaṁ karonti, aṅgarāgamukharāgaṁ karonti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six used facial ointments, applied facial creams, powdered their face, applied rouge to their face, wore cosmetics on the body, wore cosmetics on the face, and wore cosmetics on the body and face. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, mukhaṁ ālimpitabbaṁ …pe… na mukhaṁ ummadditabbaṁ, na mukhaṁ cuṇṇetabbaṁ, na manosilikāya mukhaṁ lañchetabbaṁ, na aṅgarāgo kātabbo, na mukharāgo kātabbo, na aṅgarāgamukharāgo kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use facial ointments, apply facial creams, powder your face, apply rouge to your face, wear cosmetics on the body, wear cosmetics on the face, or wear cosmetics on the body and face. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno cakkhurogābādho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards a certain monk had an eye disease.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā mukhaṁ ālimpitun”ti.
text: “I allow facial ointments for those who are sick.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe giraggasamajjo hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū giraggasamajjaṁ dassanāya agamaṁsu. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā naccampi gītampi vāditampi dassanāya gacchissanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion in Rājagaha there was a hilltop fair, and the monks from the group of six went to see it. People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics go and see dancing, singing, and music? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” They told the Buddha.
title: Entertainment, etc.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, naccaṁ vā gītaṁ vā vāditaṁ vā dassanāya gantabbaṁ. Yo gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t go and see dancing, singing, and music. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṁ gāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “yatheva mayaṁ gāyāma, evamevime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṁ gāyantī”ti. Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṁ gāyissantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six were singing the Teaching with a drawn-out voice. People complained and criticized them, “These Sakyan monastics sing with a drawn-out voice just like we do.” The monks heard the complaints of those people, and the monks of few desires complained and criticized them, “How can the monks from the group of six sing like this?” They told the Buddha.

original: “Saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave …pe… “saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti …pe… dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: “Is it true, monks, that the monks from the group of six are singing like this?” “It’s true, sir.” … the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

original: “pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṁ gāyantassa. Attanāpi tasmiṁ sare sārajjati, parepi tasmiṁ sare sārajjanti, gahapatikāpi ujjhāyanti, sarakuttimpi nikāmayamānassa samādhissa bhaṅgo hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjati—
text: “There are these five drawbacks to singing the Teaching with a drawn-out voice: one delights in the sound; others delight in the sound; householders criticize it; when one who takes pleasure in performing with the voice, one’s stillness is disrupted; later generations follow one’s example.

original: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṁ gāyantassa.
Na, bhikkhave, āyatakena gītassarena dhammo gāyitabbo. Yo gāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: You shouldn’t sing the Teaching with a drawn-out voice. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sarabhaññe kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Being afraid of wrongdoing, the monks did not chant. They told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sarabhaññan”ti.
text: “I allow chanting.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bāhiralomiṁ uṇṇiṁ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six wore fleecy woolen robes with fleece on the outside. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, bāhiyalomi uṇṇi dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t wear a fleecy woolen robe with fleece on the outside. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa ārāme ambā phalino honti. Raññā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārena anuññātaṁ hoti— “yathāsukhaṁ ayyā ambaṁ paribhuñjantū”ti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū taruṇaññeva ambaṁ pātāpetvā paribhuñjiṁsu. Rañño ca māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa ambena attho hoti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro manusse āṇāpesi— “gacchatha, bhaṇe, ārāmaṁ gantvā ambaṁ āharathā”ti. “Evaṁ, devā”ti kho te manussā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paṭissutvā ārāmaṁ gantvā ārāmapālaṁ etadavocuṁ— “devassa, bhaṇe, ambena attho, ambaṁ dethā”ti.
text: On one occasion when the mango trees in King Bimbisāra’s park were bearing fruit, the king allowed the monks to eat as many mangoes as they wished. The monks from the group of six plucked and ate them all, even the unripe ones. Just then the king needed mangoes. He told his people, “Go to the park and bring back mangoes.” Saying, “Yes, sir,” they went to the park and said to the park keeper, “The king needs mangoes. Please get some.”
title: Fruit

original: “Natthāyyā, ambaṁ. Taruṇaññeva ambaṁ pātāpetvā bhikkhū paribhuñjiṁsū”ti.
text: “There aren’t any. The monks plucked and ate them all, including the unripe ones.”

original: Atha kho te manussā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ. “Suparibhuttaṁ, bhaṇe, ayyehi ambaṁ, api ca bhagavatā mattā vaṇṇitā”ti.
text: They reported it to the king. He said, “It’s good that the venerables have eaten the mangoes. Still, the Buddha has praised moderation.”

original: Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā na mattaṁ jānitvā rañño ambaṁ paribhuñjissantī”ti. Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: People complained and criticized them, “How can the Sakyan monastics eat the king’s mangoes without moderation?” The monks heard the complaints of those people and then told the Buddha.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, ambaṁ paribhuñjitabbaṁ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t eat mangoes. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṁ hoti. Sūpe ambapesikāyo pakkhittā honti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nappaṭiggaṇhanti …pe…
text: Soon afterwards a certain association was offering a meal to the Sangha. They had prepared mango curry. Being afraid of wrongdoing, the monks did not accept it.

original: “paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjatha. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ambapesikan”ti.
text: “Accept, monks, and eat it. I allow pieces of mango.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṁ hoti. Te na pariyāpuṇiṁsu ambapesikaṁ kātuṁ, bhattagge sakaleheva ambehi denti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nappaṭiggaṇhanti.
text: Soon afterwards a certain association was offering a meal to the Sangha. They were unable to prepare mango pieces and so gave whole mangoes in the dining hall. Being afraid of wrongdoing, the monks did not accept them.

original: “Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjatha. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṁ paribhuñjituṁ— aggiparicitaṁ, satthaparicitaṁ, nakhaparicitaṁ, abījaṁ, nibbattabījaññeva pañcamaṁ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṁ paribhuñjitun”ti.
text: “Accept, monks, and eat it. I allow you to eat fruit that’s allowable for monastics for any of five reasons: it’s been damaged by fire, a knife, or a fingernail, or it’s seedless, or the seeds have been removed.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅkato hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion a monk had been bitten by a snake and died. They told the Buddha.
title: Protection

original: “Na hi nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phari. Sace hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phareyya, na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṁ kareyya. Katamāni cattāri ahirājakulāni? Virūpakkhaṁ ahirājakulaṁ, erāpathaṁ ahirājakulaṁ, chabyāputtaṁ ahirājakulaṁ, kaṇhāgotamaṁ ahirājakulaṁ. Na hi nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phari. Sace hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phareyya, na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṁ kareyya. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena pharituṁ, attaguttiyā attarakkhāya attaparittaṁ kātuṁ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbaṁ—
text: “That monk hadn’t spread good will to the four royal snake clans. Had he done so, he wouldn’t have died. What are the four clans? The Virūpakkhas, the Erāpathas, the Chabyāputtas, and the Kaṇhāgotamas. To protect yourselves, monks, you should spread good will to these four royal snake clans. And it should be done like this:

original:
‘Virūpakkhehi me mettaṁ,
Mettaṁ erāpathehi me;
Chabyāputtehi me mettaṁ,
Mettaṁ kaṇhāgotamakehi ca.
text:
I have good will toward the Virūpakkhas,
Toward the Erāpathas I have good will;
I have good will toward the Chabyāputtas,
And toward the Kaṇhāgotamas.

original:
Apādakehi me mettaṁ,
mettaṁ dvipādakehi me;
Catuppadehi me mettaṁ,
mettaṁ bahuppadehi me.
text:
I have good will toward the legless,
Toward the two-legged I have good will;
I have good will toward the four-legged,
And toward the many-legged.

original:
Mā maṁ apādako hiṁsi,
mā maṁ hiṁsi dvipādako;
Mā maṁ catuppado hiṁsi,
mā maṁ hiṁsi bahuppado.
text:
May the legless not hurt me,
May the two-legged not hurt me.
May the four-legged not hurt me,
May the many-legged not hurt me.

original:
Sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā,
sabbe bhūtā ca kevalā;
Sabbe bhadrāni passantu,
mā kiñci pāpamāgamā.
text:
All beings, all creatures,
All living beings everywhere,
May they all have good fortune,
May none meet with anything bad.

original:
Appamāṇo buddho,
Appamāṇo dhammo;
Appamāṇo saṅgho,
Pamāṇavantāni sarīsapāni.
text:
The Buddha is unlimited,
The Teaching is unlimited,
The Sangha is unlimited.
But creeping animals are limited:

Snakes, scorpions, centipedes,
Spiders, lizards, and mice.
I’m now protected and guarded;
May the creatures turn back.
I pay homage to the Buddha,
To the seven fully awakened Buddhas.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu anabhiratiyā pīḷito attano aṅgajātaṁ chindi. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ. “Aññamhi so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso chetabbamhi, aññaṁ chindi.
text: On one occasion a monk who was plagued by lust cut off his own penis. They told the Buddha. He said, “This fool has cut off one thing, when he should’ve cut off something else.

original: Na, bhikkhave, attano aṅgajātaṁ chetabbaṁ. Yo chindeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.
text: You shouldn’t cut off your own penis. If you do, you commit a serious offense.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa mahagghassa candanassa candanagaṇṭhi uppannā hoti. Atha kho rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa etadahosi— “yannūnāhaṁ imāya candanagaṇṭhiyā pattaṁ lekhāpeyyaṁ. Lekhañca me paribhogaṁ bhavissati, pattañca dānaṁ dassāmī”ti. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhi tāya candanagaṇṭhiyā pattaṁ lekhāpetvā sikkāya uḍḍitvā veḷagge ālaggetvā veḷuparamparāya bandhitvā evamāha— “yo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā arahā ceva iddhimā ca dinnaṁyeva pattaṁ oharatū”ti.
text: On one occasion a wealthy merchant of Rājagaha had obtained a valuable block of sandalwood. He thought, “Why don’t I have a bowl carved from this block of sandal? I’d use the chips myself, but give the bowl away as a gift.” He then had a bowl carved, put it in a carrying net, hung it at the end of a succession of vertical bamboo poles, and announced, “I’ll give this bowl to any perfected monastic or brahmin who brings it down by supernormal power.”
title: Bowls

original: Atha kho pūraṇo kassapo yena rājagahako seṭṭhi tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājagahakaṁ seṭṭhiṁ etadavoca— “ahañhi, gahapati, arahā ceva iddhimā ca, dehi me pattan”ti.
text: Pūraṇa Kassapa went to that merchant and said, “I’m perfected and have supernormal powers. Give me the bowl.”

original: “Sace, bhante, āyasmā arahā ceva iddhimā ca dinnaṁyeva pattaṁ oharatū”ti.
text: “If you’re perfected and have supernormal powers, then bring it down and it’s yours.”

original: Atha kho makkhali gosālo … ajito kesakambalo … pakudho kaccāyano … sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto … nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto yena rājagahako seṭṭhi tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājagahakaṁ seṭṭhiṁ etadavoca— “ahañhi, gahapati, arahā ceva iddhimā ca, dehi me pattan”ti. “Sace, bhante, āyasmā arahā ceva iddhimā ca, dinnaṁyeva pattaṁ oharatū”ti.
text: The same thing happened with Makkhali Gosāla, Ajita Kesakambala, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañcaya Belaṭṭhaputta, and the Jain ascetic from Ñātika.

original: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā ca piṇḍolabhāradvājo pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṁ piṇḍāya pavisiṁsu. Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca— “āyasmā kho mahāmoggallāno arahā ceva iddhimā ca. Gacchāvuso, moggallāna, etaṁ pattaṁ ohara. Tuyheso patto”ti.
text: Soon afterwards, after robing up in the morning, Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja took their bowls and robes and entered Rājagaha for alms. Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja said to Mahāmoggallāna, “Venerable, you’re perfected and have supernormal powers. If you go and bring down that bowl, it’s yours.”

original: “Āyasmā kho bhāradvājo arahā ceva iddhimā ca. Gacchāvuso, bhāradvāja, etaṁ pattaṁ ohara. Tuyheso patto”ti.
text: “Venerable, you too are perfected and have supernormal powers. If you bring it down, it’s yours.”

original: Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo vehāsaṁ abbhuggantvā taṁ pattaṁ gahetvā tikkhattuṁ rājagahaṁ anupariyāyi.
text: Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja then rose into the air, took hold of that bowl, and circled around Rājagaha three times.

original: Tena kho pana samayena rājagahako seṭṭhi saputtadāro sake nivesane ṭhito hoti pañjaliko namassamāno— idheva, bhante, ayyo bhāradvājo amhākaṁ nivesane patiṭṭhātūti. Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa nivesane patiṭṭhāsi. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhi āyasmato piṇḍolabhāradvājassa hatthato pattaṁ gahetvā mahagghassa khādanīyassa pūretvā āyasmato piṇḍolabhāradvājassa adāsi. Atha kho āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo taṁ pattaṁ gahetvā ārāmaṁ agamāsi.
text: Just then that merchant, together with his wives and children, was standing in his own house, raising his joined palms in homage, thinking, “May Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja land right here at our house.” And Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja did just that. The merchant then took the bowl from his hands, filled it with expensive fresh foods, and gave it back to Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja, who then left for the monastery.

original: Assosuṁ kho manussā— ayyena kira piṇḍolabhāradvājena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohāritoti. Te ca manussā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā āyasmantaṁ piṇḍolabhāradvājaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhiṁsu. Assosi kho bhagavā uccāsaddaṁ mahāsaddaṁ; sutvāna āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi— “kiṁ nu kho so, ānanda, uccāsaddo mahāsaddo”ti? “Āyasmatā, bhante, piṇḍolabhāradvājena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohārito. Assosuṁ kho, bhante, manussā— ayyena kira piṇḍolabhāradvājena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohāritoti. Te ca, bhante, manussā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā āyasmantaṁ piṇḍolabhāradvājaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā. So eso, bhante, bhagavā uccāsaddo mahāsaddo”ti.
text: People heard that Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja had taken down the merchant’s bowl, and making a great uproar, they followed right behind him. Hearing all the noise, the Buddha asked Venerable Ānanda what it was, and Ānanda told him what had happened.

original: Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṁ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṁ piṇḍolabhāradvājaṁ paṭipucchi— “saccaṁ kira tayā, bhāradvāja, rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa patto ohārito”ti?
text: Soon afterwards the Buddha had the Sangha of monks gathered and questioned Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja: “Is it true, Bhāradvāja, that you brought down that merchant’s bowl?”

original: “Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.
text: “It’s true, sir.”

original: Vigarahi buddho bhagavā— “ananucchavikaṁ, bhāradvāja, ananulomikaṁ appatirūpaṁ assāmaṇakaṁ akappiyaṁ akaraṇīyaṁ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṁ, bhāradvāja, chavassa dārupattassa kāraṇā gihīnaṁ uttari manussadhammaṁ iddhipāṭihāriyaṁ dassessasi. Seyyathāpi, bhāradvāja, mātugāmo chavassa māsakarūpassa kāraṇā kopinaṁ dasseti; evameva kho tayā, bhāradvāja, chavassa dārupattassa kāraṇā gihīnaṁ uttari manussadhammaṁ iddhipāṭihāriyaṁ dassitaṁ. Netaṁ, bhāradvāja, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe… vigarahitvā …pe… dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: The Buddha rebuked him, “It’s not suitable, Bhāradvāja, it’s not proper, it’s not worthy of a monastic, it’s not allowable, it’s not to be done. How could you show a superhuman ability, a wonder of supernormal power, to householders for the sake of a miserable wooden bowl? It’s just like a woman showing her private parts for a miserable māsaka coin. This will affect people’s confidence …” After rebuking him … the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

original: “na, bhikkhave, gihīnaṁ uttarimanussadhammaṁ iddhipāṭihāriyaṁ dassetabbaṁ. Yo dasseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.
text: “You shouldn’t show a superhuman ability, a wonder of supernormal power, to householders. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.

original: Bhindathetaṁ, bhikkhave, dārupattaṁ sakalikaṁ sakalikaṁ katvā, bhikkhūnaṁ añjanupapisanaṁ detha.
text: Now destroy that wooden bowl and turn it into splinters. Give these to the monks to use as scent in ointments.

original: Na ca, bhikkhave, dārupatto dhāretabbo. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: And you shouldn’t use a wooden bowl. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvace patte dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṁ rūpiyamayaṁ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six used luxurious bowls made with gold and silver. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, sovaṇṇamayo patto dhāretabbo …pe… na rūpiyamayo patto dhāretabbo … na maṇimayo patto dhāretabbo … na veḷuriyamayo patto dhāretabbo … na phalikamayo patto dhāretabbo … na kaṁsamayo patto dhāretabbo … na kācamayo patto dhāretabbo … na tipumayo patto dhāretabbo … na sīsamayo patto dhāretabbo … na tambalohamayo patto dhāretabbo. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve patte— ayopattaṁ, mattikāpattan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use almsbowls made with gold, silver, gems, beryl, crystal, bronze, glass, tin, lead, or copper. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow two kinds of almsbowls: iron bowls and ceramic bowls.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena pattamūlaṁ ghaṁsiyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the bottoms of the bowls became scratched.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattamaṇḍalan”ti.
text: “I allow a circular bowl rest.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṁ rūpiyamayaṁ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards the monks from the group of six used luxurious bowl rests made with gold and silver. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhāretabbāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve pattamaṇḍalāni— tipumayaṁ, sīsamayan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use luxurious bowl rests. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow two kinds of bowl rests: bowl-rests made of tin and a bowl-rests made of lead.”

original: Bahalāni maṇḍalāni na acchupiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There were thick bowl rests on which the bowls did not sit properly.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, likhitun”ti.
text: “I allow you to carve them out.”

original: Valī honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There were marks left from the carving.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, makaradantakaṁ chinditun”ti.
text: “I allow you to cut a shark-teeth pattern.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū citrāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhārenti rūpakākiṇṇāni bhittikammakatāni. Tāni rathikāyapi dassentā āhiṇḍanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon the monks from the group of six used colorful bowl rests, decorated like walls. As they were walking about, they showed them off in the streets. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, citrāni pattamaṇḍalāni dhāretabbāni rūpakākiṇṇāni bhittikammakatāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pakatimaṇḍalan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use colorful bowl rests, decorated like a wall. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow ordinary bowl rests.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sodakaṁ pattaṁ paṭisāmenti. Patto dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At this time there were monks who put away their bowls while still wet. The bowls were stained.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, sodako patto paṭisāmetabbo. Yo paṭisāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, otāpetvā pattaṁ paṭisāmetun”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t put away your bowl while still wet. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. You should sun your bowl and then put it away.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sodakaṁ pattaṁ otāpenti. Patto duggandho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards there were monks who sunned their bowls while still wet. The bowls became smelly.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, sodako patto otāpetabbo. Yo otāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vodakaṁ katvā otāpetvā pattaṁ paṭisāmetun”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t sun your bowl while still wet. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. You should dry the bowl and then sun it before you put it away.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū uṇhe pattaṁ nidahanti. Pattassa vaṇṇo dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Monks left their bowls in the heat of the sun. The bowls became discolored.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Yo nidaheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, muhuttaṁ uṇhe otāpetvā pattaṁ paṭisāmetun”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t leave your bowl in the heat of the sun. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. You should sun it in the heat for a short time and then put it away.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā pattā ajjhokāse anādhārā nikkhittā honti. Vātamaṇḍalikāya āvaṭṭetvā pattā bhijjiṁsu. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion a number of almsbowls had been put down outside without support. A whirlwind rolled the bowls around and as a result they broke.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattādhārakan”ti.
text: “I allow a bowl rack.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū miḍḍhante pattaṁ nikkhipanti. Paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion there were monks who had put their bowls on the edge of a bench. They fell down and broke.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, miḍḍhante patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t put your almsbowl on the edge of a bench. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū paribhaṇḍante pattaṁ nikkhipanti. Paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion there were monks who had put their bowls on the edge of a ledge. They fell down and broke.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, paribhaṇḍante patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t put your almsbowl on the edge of a ledge. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chamāya pattaṁ nikkujjanti. Oṭṭho ghaṁsiyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks put their bowls upside down on the ground. The edges of the bowls were scratched.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇasanthārakan”ti.
text: “I allow a spread of grass.”

original: Tiṇasanthārako upacikāhi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The grass was eaten by termites.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, coḷakan”ti.
text: “I allow a cloth.”

original: Coḷakaṁ upacikāhi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The cloth was eaten by termites.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattamāḷakan”ti.
text: “I allow a platform for bowls.”

original: Pattamāḷako paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The bowls fell off the platform and broke.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattakuṇḍolikan”ti.
text: “I allow a storage container for almsbowls.”

original: Pattakuṇḍolikāya patto ghaṁsiyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The bowls were scratched in the storage containers.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pattatthavikan”ti.
text: “I allow a bowl bag.”

original: Aṁsabaddhako na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There were no shoulder straps.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṁsabaddhakaṁ bandhanasuttakan”ti.
text: “I allow a shoulder strap and a string for fastening.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhittikhilepi nāgadantakepi pattaṁ laggenti. Paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who hung their bowls from wall pegs. The bowls fell down and broke.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, patto laggetabbo. Yo laggeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t hang up your almsbowl. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū mañce pattaṁ nikkhipanti, satisammosā nisīdantā ottharitvā pattaṁ bhindenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who placed their bowls on beds. Sitting down absentmindedly, they crushed the bowls, breaking them.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, mañce patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t place your bowl on a bed. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū pīṭhe pattaṁ nikkhipanti, satisammosā nisīdantā ottharitvā pattaṁ bhindenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time monks placed their bowls on benches. Sitting down absentmindedly, they crushed the bowls, breaking them.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, pīṭhe patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t place your bowl on a bench. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū aṅke pattaṁ nikkhipanti, satisammosā uṭṭhahanti. Paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who put their bowls in their laps. When they got up absentmindedly, the bowls fell down and broke.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, aṅke patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t put your bowl in your lap. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chatte pattaṁ nikkhipanti. Vātamaṇḍalikāya chattaṁ ukkhipiyati paripatitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At one time there were monks who put their bowls on a sunshade. A whirlwind lifted the sunshade, and the bowls fell down and broke.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, chatte patto nikkhipitabbo. Yo nikkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t put your bowl on a sunshade. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū pattahatthā kavāṭaṁ paṇāmenti. Kavāṭo āvaṭṭitvā patto bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who opened doors with a bowl in their hand. The doors swung back and the bowls broke.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, pattahatthena kavāṭaṁ paṇāmetabbaṁ. Yo paṇāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t open a door with an almsbowl in your hand. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū tumbakaṭāhe piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi titthiyā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who walked for alms with gourds as bowls. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like the monastics of other religions.”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, tumbakaṭāhe piṇḍāya caritabbaṁ. Yo careyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t walk for alms with a gourd as a bowl. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ghaṭikaṭāhe piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi titthiyā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who walked for alms with waterpots as bowls. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like the monastics of other religions.”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, ghaṭikaṭāhe piṇḍāya caritabbaṁ. Yo careyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t walk for alms with a waterpot as a bowl. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sabbapaṁsukūliko hoti. So chavasīsassa pattaṁ dhāreti. Aññatarā itthī passitvā bhītā vissaramakāsi— “abhuṁ me pisāco vatāyan”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā chavasīsassa pattaṁ dhāressanti, seyyathāpi pisācillikā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time a certain monk who only used discarded things used a skull as a bowl. A woman who saw this was terrified, screaming, “Oh my God, a demon!” People complained and criticized him, “How can the Sakyan monastics use skulls as bowls? They’re just like goblins.”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, chavasīsassa patto dhāretabbo. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, sabbapaṁsukūlikena bhavitabbaṁ. Yo bhaveyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use a skull as a bowl. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. And you shouldn’t use only discarded things. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū calakānipi aṭṭhikānipi ucchiṭṭhodakampi pattena nīharanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “yasmiṁ yevime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā bhuñjanti sova nesaṁ paṭiggaho”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who carried away chewed food remnants, bones, and wastewater in their bowls. People complained and criticized them, “These Sakyan monastics use the vessel they’re eating from as a trash can.”

original: “Na bhikkhave, calakāni vā aṭṭhikāni vā ucchiṭṭhodakaṁ vā pattena nīharitabbaṁ. Yo nīhareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭiggahan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t carry away chewed food remnants, bones, and wastewater in your almsbowl. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow trash cans.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū hatthena vipphāḷetvā cīvaraṁ sibbenti. Cīvaraṁ vilomikaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks tore cloth to pieces by hand and then sewed robes. The robes were ugly. They told the Buddha.
title: Robe making

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, satthakaṁ namatakan”ti.
text: “I allow a knife and a felt sheath.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa daṇḍasatthakaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards the Sangha was offered a knife with a handle.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, daṇḍasatthakan”ti.
text: “I allow a knife with a handle.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvace satthakadaṇḍe dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṁ rūpiyamayaṁ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At this time the monks from the group of six used luxurious knife handles made with gold and silver. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā satthakadaṇḍā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṁ dantamayaṁ visāṇamayaṁ naḷamayaṁ veḷumayaṁ kaṭṭhamayaṁ jatumayaṁ phalamayaṁ lohamayaṁ saṅkhanābhimayan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use luxurious knife handles. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow knife handles made of bone, ivory, horn, reed, bamboo, wood, resin, fruit, metal, or shell.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kukkuṭapattenapi veḷupesikāyapi cīvaraṁ sibbenti. Cīvaraṁ dussibbitaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks used chicken feathers and pieces of bamboo to sew robes. The robes were badly sewn.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sūcin”ti.
text: “I allow needles.”

original: Sūciyo kaṇṇakitāyo honti …pe…
text: The needles rusted.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sūcināḷikan”ti.
text: “I allow a cylinder for the needles.”

original: Sūcināḷikāyapi kaṇṇakitāyo honti …pe…
text: The needles still rusted.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kiṇṇena pūretun”ti.
text: “I allow you to fill them with yeast.”

original: Kiṇṇepi kaṇṇakitāyo honti …pe…
text: The needles still rusted.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattuyā pūretun”ti.
text: “I allow you to fill them with flour.”

original: Sattuyāpi kaṇṇakitāyo honti …pe…
text: The needles still rusted.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saritakan”ti.
text: “I allow stone powder.”

original: Saritakepi kaṇṇakitāyo honti …pe…
text: The needles still rusted.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, madhusitthakena sāretun”ti.
text: “I allow you to mix it with beeswax.”

original: Saritakaṁ paribhijjati …pe…
text: The stone powder broke apart.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saritakasipāṭikan”ti.
text: “I allow a case.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū tattha tattha khilaṁ nikkhaṇitvā sambandhitvā cīvaraṁ sibbenti. Cīvaraṁ vikaṇṇaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks erected posts here and there, bound them together, and sewed robes. The corners of the robes were deformed. They told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinaṁ kathinarajjuṁ tattha tattha obandhitvā cīvaraṁ sibbetun”ti.
text: “I allow a frame and a string. You should tie down the cloth to the frame as required, before sewing the robe.”

original: Visame kathinaṁ pattharanti. Kathinaṁ paribhijjati …pe…
text: They laid the frame on uneven ground. The frame broke.

original: “na, bhikkhave, visame kathinaṁ pattharitabbaṁ. Yo patthareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t lay the frame on uneven ground. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Chamāya kathinaṁ pattharanti. Kathinaṁ paṁsukitaṁ hoti …pe…
text: They laid the frame on the ground. The frame got dirty.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇasanthārakan”ti.
text: “I allow a spread of grass.”

original: Kathinassa anto jīrati …pe…
text: The edges of the frame deteriorated.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anuvātaṁ paribhaṇḍaṁ āropetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to add an edge lengthwise and crosswise.”

original: Kathinaṁ nappahoti …pe…
text: The frame was not the right size.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, daṇḍakathinaṁ bidalakaṁ salākaṁ vinandhanarajjuṁ vinandhanasuttaṁ vinandhitvā cīvaraṁ sibbetun”ti.
text: “I allow an inner frame, folding a straw mat to fit the frame, spacers, strings for tying together, and strings for tying down. After tying it together, you should sew the robe.”

original: Suttantarikāyo visamā honti …pe…
text: The seams were unevenly spaced.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kaḷimbhakan”ti.
text: “I allow a ruler.”

original: Suttā vaṅkā honti …pe…
text: The seams were not straight.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, moghasuttakan”ti.
text: “I allow you to make a guide line.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū adhotehi pādehi kathinaṁ akkamanti. Kathinaṁ dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There were monks who stepped on the frame with dirty feet. The frame got dirty.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, adhotehi pādehi kathinaṁ akkamitabbaṁ. Yo akkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t step on the frame with dirty feet. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū allehi pādehi kathinaṁ akkamanti. Kathinaṁ dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There were monks who stepped on the frame with wet feet. The frame got dirty.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, allehi pādehi kathinaṁ akkamitabbaṁ. Yo akkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t step on the frame with wet feet. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū saupāhanā kathinaṁ akkamanti. Kathinaṁ dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There were monks who stepped on the frame while wearing sandals. The frame got dirty.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, saupāhanena kathinaṁ akkamitabbaṁ. Yo akkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t step on the frame while wearing sandals. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū cīvaraṁ sibbantā aṅguliyā paṭiggaṇhanti. Aṅguliyo dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: When sewing robes, the monks used their bare fingers. They pricked their fingers.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭiggahan”ti.
text: “I allow thimbles.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvace paṭiggahe dhārenti sovaṇṇamayaṁ rūpiyamayaṁ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon the monks from the group of six used luxurious thimbles made with gold and silver. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā paṭiggahā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṁ …pe… saṅkhanābhimayan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use luxurious thimbles. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow a thimble made of bone, ivory, horn, reed, bamboo, wood, resin, fruit, metal, or shell.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena sūciyopi satthakāpi paṭiggahāpi nassanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Needles, knives, and thimbles got lost.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āvesanavitthakan”ti.
text: “I allow a small bowl.”

original: Āvesanavitthake samākulā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The small bowls became crowded.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭiggahathavikan”ti.
text: “I allow a bag for thimbles.”

original: Aṁsabaddhako na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There was no shoulder strap.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṁsabaddhakaṁ bandhanasuttakan”ti.
text: “I allow a shoulder strap and a string for fastening.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū abbhokāse cīvaraṁ sibbantā sītenapi uṇhenapi kilamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: When sewing robes outside, the monks were troubled by the cold and heat. They told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinasālaṁ kathinamaṇḍapan”ti.
text: “I allow sewing sheds and roof covers.”

original: Kathinasālā nīcavatthukā hoti, udakena otthariyyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: They built the sewing shed on a low base. It was flooded.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṁ kātun”ti.
text: “I allow you to raise the base.”

original: Cayo paripatati …pe…
text: The mound collapsed.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṁ tayo caye— iṭṭhakācayaṁ, silācayaṁ, dārucayan”ti.
text: “I allow you to construct three kinds of raised foundations: raised foundations of brick, stone, and wood.”

original: Ārohantā vihaññanti …pe…
text: It was difficult to get up to the sewing sheds.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne— iṭṭhakāsopānaṁ, silāsopānaṁ, dārusopānan”ti.
text: “I allow three kinds of stairs: stairs of brick, stone, and wood.”

original: Ārohantā paripatanti …pe…
text: People fell down while climbing the stairs.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāhan”ti.
text: “I allow rails.”

original: Kathinasālāya tiṇacuṇṇaṁ paripatati …pe…
text: Grass and dust fell into the sewing sheds.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṁ kātuṁ— setavaṇṇaṁ kāḷavaṇṇaṁ gerukaparikammaṁ mālākammaṁ latākammaṁ makaradantakaṁ pañcapaṭikaṁ cīvaravaṁsaṁ cīvararajjukan”ti.
text: “I allow you to firm up the structure and then to plaster it inside and outside, including: treating with white color, black color, and red ocher; making garland patterns, creeper patterns, shark-teeth patterns, and the fivefold pattern; putting up bamboo robe racks and clotheslines.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū cīvaraṁ sibbetvā tattheva kathinaṁ ujjhitvā pakkamanti, undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time, when they had finished sewing a robe, there were monks who abandoned the frame right there and left. Rats and termites ate it.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinaṁ saṅgharitun”ti.
text: “You should fold up the frame.”

original: Kathinaṁ paribhijjati …pe…
text: The frame broke.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, goghaṁsikāya kathinaṁ saṅgharitun”ti.
text: “You should fold it up with a rod for support.”

original: Kathinaṁ viniveṭhiyati …pe…
text: The frame unfolded.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bandhanarajjun”ti.
text: “You should tie it up with a rope.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kuṭṭepi thambhepi kathinaṁ ussāpetvā pakkamanti. Paripatitvā kathinaṁ bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time there were monks who leaned the frame against a wall or a pillar and left. It fell down and broke.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhittikhile vā nāgadante vā laggetun”ti.
text: “You should hang it from a wall peg.”

original: Atha kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṁ viharitvā yena vesālī tena cārikaṁ pakkāmi. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sūcikampi satthakampi bhesajjampi pattena ādāya gacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: When the Buddha had stayed at Rājagaha for as long as he liked, he set out wandering toward Vesālī. And so did the monks, having put their needles, knives, and medicines in their almsbowls. They told the Buddha.
title: Various allowable requisites

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhesajjatthavikan”ti.
text: “I allow a medicine bag.”

original: Aṁsabaddhako na hoti …pe…
text: There was no shoulder strap.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṁsabaddhakaṁ bandhanasuttakan”ti.
text: “I allow a shoulder strap and a string for fastening it.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu upāhanāyo kāyabandhanena bandhitvā gāmaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Aññataro upāsako taṁ bhikkhuṁ abhivādento upāhanāyo sīsena ghaṭṭeti. So bhikkhu maṅku ahosi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṁ gantvā bhikkhūnaṁ etamatthaṁ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion a certain monk bound his sandals to his belt and entered the village for alms. A lay follower who bowed to him hit his head against those sandals. The monk was embarrassed. When he had returned to the monastery, he told the monks what had happened, who in turn told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upāhanatthavikan”ti.
text: “I allow a bag for sandals.”

original: Aṁsabaddhako na hoti …pe…
text: There was no shoulder strap.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṁsabaddhakaṁ bandhanasuttakan”ti.
text: “I allow a shoulder strap and a string for fastening it.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena antarāmagge udakaṁ akappiyaṁ hoti. Parissāvanaṁ na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: While they were traveling, there was only unallowable water, but no water filter.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parissāvanan”ti.
text: “I allow a water filter.”

original: Coḷakaṁ nappahoti …pe…
text: There was no suitable cloth.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kaṭacchuparissāvanan”ti.
text: “I allow a filter with a handle.”

original: Coḷakaṁ nappahoti …pe…
text: There was still no suitable cloth.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhammakaraṇan”ti.
text: “I allow a water strainer.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena dve bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Eko bhikkhu anācāraṁ ācarati. Dutiyo bhikkhu taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca— “mā, āvuso, evarūpaṁ akāsi. Netaṁ kappatī”ti. So tasmiṁ upanandhi.
text: On one occasion, there were two monks traveling through the Kosalan country. One monk misbehaved, and the other monk said to him, “Don’t do that. It’s not allowable.” Because of that, the first monk became resentful.

original: Atha kho so bhikkhu pipāsāya pīḷito upanaddhaṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca— “dehi me, āvuso, parissāvanaṁ, pānīyaṁ pivissāmī”ti. Upanaddho bhikkhu na adāsi. So bhikkhu pipāsāya pīḷito kālamakāsi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṁ gantvā bhikkhūnaṁ etamatthaṁ ārocesi.
text: Soon afterwards the other monk was very thirsty. He asked the resentful monk to borrow his water filter. He refused and the other monk died from thirst. When the resentful monk arrived at the monastery, he told the monks what had happened.

original: “Kiṁ pana tvaṁ, āvuso, parissāvanaṁ yāciyamāno na adāsī”ti?
text: “So you refused to lend your water filter when asked?”

original: “Evamāvuso”ti.
text: “Yes.”

original: Ye te bhikkhū appicchā …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu parissāvanaṁ yāciyamāno na dassatī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṁ sannipātāpetvā taṁ bhikkhuṁ paṭipucchi—
text: The monks of few desires complained and criticized him, “How could a monk do such a thing?” They told the Buddha. Soon afterwards the Buddha had the monks gathered and questioned that monk:

original: “saccaṁ kira tvaṁ, bhikkhu, parissāvanaṁ yāciyamāno na adāsī”ti?
text: “Is it true, monk, that you did this?”

original: “Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.
text: “It’s true, sir.”

original: Vigarahi buddho bhagavā— “ananucchavikaṁ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṁ appatirūpaṁ assāmaṇakaṁ akappiyaṁ akaraṇīyaṁ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṁ, moghapurisa, parissāvanaṁ yāciyamāno na dassasi. Netaṁ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe… vigarahitvā …pe… dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: The Buddha rebuked him, “It’s not suitable, foolish man, it’s not proper, it’s not worthy of a monastic, it’s not allowable, it’s not to be done. How could you refuse to lend your water filter when asked? This will affect people’s confidence …” After rebuking him … the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

original: “na, bhikkhave, addhānamaggappaṭipannena bhikkhunā parissāvanaṁ yāciyamānena na dātabbaṁ. Yo na dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, aparissāvanakena addhāno paṭipajjitabbo. Yo paṭipajjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sace na hoti parissāvanaṁ vā dhammakaraṇo vā, saṅghāṭikaṇṇopi adhiṭṭhātabbo— iminā parissāvetvā pivissāmī”ti.
text: “If you’re traveling with a monk and he asks to borrow your water filter, you should lend it. If you don’t, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. On the other hand, you shouldn’t travel without a water filter. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. If there’s no water filter or strainer, you should determine a corner of your robe: ‘I’ll drink after filtering with this.’”

original: Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṁ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū navakammaṁ karonti. Parissāvanaṁ na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Buddha eventually arrived at Vesālī where he stayed in the house with the peaked roof in the Great Wood. At this time the monks were doing building work, but there were not enough water filters. They told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, daṇḍaparissāvanan”ti.
text: “I allow a water filter of cloth fitted to a wooden framework.”

original: Daṇḍaparissāvanaṁ na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: There were still not enough filters.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ottharakan”ti.
text: “I allow you to filter by spreading cloth on water.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū makasehi ubbāḷhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At this time the monks were troubled by mosquitoes.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, makasakuṭikan”ti.
text: “I allow a mosquito tent.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena vesāliyaṁ paṇītānaṁ bhattānaṁ bhattapaṭipāṭi aṭṭhitā hoti. Bhikkhū paṇītāni bhojanāni bhuñjitvā abhisannakāyā honti bahvābādhā.
text: At this time in Vesālī people had arranged a succession of fine meals. After eating the fine food, the monks were often sick, their bodies being full of impurities.
title: Buildings — Walking paths

original: Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco vesāliṁ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Addasā kho jīvako komārabhacco bhikkhū abhisannakāye bahvābādhe. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavantaṁ etadavoca— “etarahi, bhante, bhikkhū abhisannakāyā bahvābādhā. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṁ caṅkamañca jantāgharañca anujānātu. Evaṁ bhikkhū appābādhā bhavissantī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā jīvakaṁ komārabhaccaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: Just then Jīvaka Komārabhacca was in Vesālī on some business, and he saw those monks. He went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down, and said, “At present, sir, there are monks who are often sick, their bodies being full of impurities. Please allow walking-meditation paths and saunas. In this way the monks will rarely get sick.” The Buddha then instructed, inspired, and gladdened him with a teaching, after which Jīvaka got up from his seat, bowed, circumambulated the Buddha with his right side toward him, and left. Soon afterwards the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:
