Te kulitthīnaṁ kuladhītānaṁ kulakumārīnaṁ kulasuṇhānaṁ kuladāsīnaṁ ekatovaṇṭikamālaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, mañjarikaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, vidhūtikaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, vaṭaṁsakaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, āveḷaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, uracchadaṁ harantipi harāpentipi.
text: They planted flowering trees, watered and plucked them, and then tied the flowers together. They made the flowers into garlands, garlands with stalks on one side and garlands with stalks on both sides. They made flower arrangements, wreaths, ornaments for the head, ornaments for the ears, and ornaments for the chest. And they had others do the same. They then took these things, or sent them, to the women, the daughters, the girls, the daughters-in-law, and the female slaves of respectable families.

original: Te kulitthīhi kuladhītāhi kulakumārīhi kulasuṇhāhi kuladāsīhi saddhiṁ ekabhājanepi bhuñjanti, ekathālakepi pivanti, ekāsanepi nisīdanti, ekamañcepi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, vikālepi bhuñjanti, majjampi pivanti, mālāgandhavilepanampi dhārenti, naccantipi, gāyantipi, vādentipi, lāsentipi; naccantiyāpi naccanti, naccantiyāpi gāyanti, naccantiyāpi vādenti, naccantiyāpi lāsenti …pe… lāsentiyāpi naccanti, lāsentiyāpi gāyanti, lāsentiyāpi vādenti, lāsentiyāpi lāsenti;
text: They ate from the same plates as these women and drank from the same vessels. They sat on the same seats as them, and they lay down on the same beds, on the same sheets, under the same covers, and both on the same sheets and under the same covers. They ate at the wrong time, drank alcohol, and wore garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics. They danced, sang, played instruments, and performed. While the women were dancing, singing, playing instruments, and performing, so would they.

original: aṭṭhapadepi kīḷanti, dasapadepi kīḷanti, ākāsepi kīḷanti, parihārapathepi kīḷanti, santikāyapi kīḷanti, khalikāyapi kīḷanti, ghaṭikāyapi kīḷanti, salākahatthenapi kīḷanti, akkhenapi kīḷanti, paṅgacīrenapi kīḷanti, vaṅkakenapi kīḷanti, mokkhacikāyapi kīḷanti, ciṅgulakenapi kīḷanti, pattāḷhakenapi kīḷanti, rathakenapi kīḷanti, dhanukenapi kīḷanti, akkharikāyapi kīḷanti, manesikāyapi kīḷanti, yathāvajjenapi kīḷanti;
text: They played various games: eight-row checkers, ten-row checkers, imaginary checkers, hopscotch, pick-up-sticks, board games, tipcat, painting with the hand, dice, leaf flutes, toy plows, somersaults, pinwheels, toy measures, toy carriages, toy bows, guessing from syllables, thought guessing, mimicking deformities.

original: hatthismimpi sikkhanti, assasmimpi sikkhanti, rathasmimpi sikkhanti, dhanusmimpi sikkhanti; tharusmimpi sikkhanti; hatthissapi purato dhāvanti, assassapi purato dhāvanti, rathassapi purato dhāvantipi ādhāvantipi; usseḷentipi, apphoṭentipi, nibbujjhantipi, muṭṭhīhipi yujjhanti; raṅgamajjhepi saṅghāṭiṁ pattharitvā naccakiṁ evaṁ vadanti— “idha, bhagini, naccassū”ti; nalāṭikampi denti; vividhampi anācāraṁ ācaranti.
text: They trained in elephant riding, in horsemanship, in carriage riding, in archery, in swordsmanship. And they ran in front of elephants, horses, and carriages, and they ran backward and forward. They whistled, clapped their hands, wrestled, and boxed. They spread their outer robe on a stage and said to the dancing girls, “Dance here, sister,” and they made gestures of approval. And they misbehaved in a variety of ways.

original: Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ …pe…
text: They told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

original: “na, bhikkhave, vividhaṁ anācāraṁ ācaritabbaṁ. Yo ācareyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

original: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmante uruvelakassape pabbajite saṅghassa bahuṁ lohabhaṇḍaṁ dārubhaṇḍaṁ mattikābhaṇḍaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṁ etadahosi— “kiṁ nu kho bhagavatā lohabhaṇḍaṁ anuññātaṁ, kiṁ ananuññātaṁ; kiṁ dārubhaṇḍaṁ anuññātaṁ, kiṁ ananuññātaṁ; kiṁ mattikābhaṇḍaṁ anuññātaṁ, kiṁ ananuññātan”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: At the time of Venerable Uruvelakassapa’s going forth, the Sangha was offered a large number of iron, wooden, and ceramic goods. The monks thought, “Which iron, wooden, and ceramic goods have been allowed by the Buddha, and which not?” They told the Buddha. The Buddha then gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā paharaṇiṁ sabbaṁ lohabhaṇḍaṁ, ṭhapetvā āsandiṁ pallaṅkaṁ dārupattaṁ dārupādukaṁ sabbaṁ dārubhaṇḍaṁ, ṭhapetvā katakañca kumbhakārikañca sabbaṁ mattikābhaṇḍan”ti.
text: “I allow all iron goods except weapons; all wooden goods except high couches, luxurious couches, wooden almsbowls, and wooden shoes; and all ceramic goods except ceramic foot scrubbers and clay huts.”

original:

original: Tena samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṁ senāsanaṁ apaññattaṁ hoti. Te ca bhikkhū tahaṁ tahaṁ viharanti— araññe, rukkhamūle, pabbate, kandarāyaṁ, giriguhāyaṁ, susāne, vanapatthe, ajjhokāse, palālapuñje. Te kālasseva tato tato upanikkhamanti— araññā rukkhamūlā pabbatā kandarā giriguhā susānā vanapatthā ajjhokāsā palālapuñjā, pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena, ālokitena vilokitena, samiñjitena pasāritena, okkhittacakkhū, iriyāpathasampannā.
text: At one time the Buddha was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrel sanctuary. At this time the Buddha had not yet allowed dwellings. As a result, the monks stayed here and there: in the wilderness, at the foot of a tree, on a hill, in a gorge, in a hillside cave, in a charnel ground, in the forest, in the open, on a heap of straw. Early in the morning, they would emerge from those places. They were pleasing in their conduct: in going out and coming back, in looking ahead and looking aside, in bending and stretching their arms. Their eyes were lowered, and they were perfect in deportment.
title: The chapter on resting places (16. Senāsanakkhandhaka) — The first section for recitation — 1. The allowance for dwellings (1.1. Vihārānujānana)

original: Tena kho pana samayena rājagahako seṭṭhī kālasseva uyyānaṁ agamāsi. Addasā kho rājagahako seṭṭhī te bhikkhū kālasseva tato tato upanikkhamante— araññā rukkhamūlā pabbatā kandarā giriguhā susānā vanapatthā ajjhokāsā palālapuñjā, pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena, ālokitena vilokitena, samiñjitena pasāritena, okkhittacakkhū, iriyāpathasampanne. Disvānassa cittaṁ pasīdi. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca— “sacāhaṁ, bhante, vihāre kārāpeyyaṁ, vaseyyātha me vihāresū”ti?
text: One morning a wealthy merchant of Rājagaha was going to a park when he saw those monks. Being inspired, he approached them and said, “If I build dwellings, sirs, would you stay in them?”

original: “Na kho, gahapati, bhagavatā vihārā anuññātā”ti.
text: “The Buddha hasn’t allowed dwellings.”

original: “Tena hi, bhante, bhagavantaṁ paṭipucchitvā mama āroceyyāthā”ti.
text: “Well then, please ask the Buddha and let me know his response.”

original: “Evaṁ, gahapatī”ti
text: “Yes.”

original: kho te bhikkhū rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ— “rājagahako, bhante, seṭṭhī vihāre kārāpetukāmo. Kathaṁ nu kho, bhante, amhehi paṭipajjitabban”ti? Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
text: Those monks then went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down, and said, “Sir, a wealthy merchant in Rājagaha wants to build dwellings. What should we do?” Soon afterwards the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca leṇāni— vihāraṁ, aḍḍhayogaṁ, pāsādaṁ, hammiyaṁ, guhan”ti.
text: “I allow five kinds of shelters: dwellings, three kinds of stilt houses, and caves.”

original: Atha kho te bhikkhū yena rājagahako seṭṭhī tenupasaṅkamiṁsu, upasaṅkamitvā rājagahakaṁ seṭṭhiṁ etadavocuṁ— “anuññātā kho, gahapati, bhagavatā vihārā; yassadāni kālaṁ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī ekāheneva saṭṭhivihāre patiṭṭhāpesi. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī te saṭṭhivihāre pariyosāpetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca— “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṁ saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavato adhivāsanaṁ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
text: The monks went to that merchant and said, “The Buddha has allowed dwellings. Please do as you think appropriate.” Then, on a single day, that merchant built sixty dwellings. When the dwellings were finished, he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down, and said, “Sir, please accept tomorrow’s meal from me together with the Sangha of monks.” The Buddha consented by remaining silent. Knowing that the Buddha had consented, he got up from his seat, bowed down, circumambulated the Buddha with his right side toward him, and left.

original: Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṁ ārocāpesi— “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṁ bhattan”ti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena rājagahakassa seṭṭhissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho rājagahako seṭṭhī buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā, bhagavantaṁ bhuttāviṁ onītapattapāṇiṁ, ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca— “ete me, bhante, saṭṭhivihārā puññatthikena saggatthikena kārāpitā. Kathāhaṁ, bhante, tesu vihāresu paṭipajjāmī”ti?
text: The next morning he had various kinds of fine foods prepared and then had the Buddha informed that the meal was ready. The Buddha robe up, took his bowl and robe, and went to the house of that merchant where he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Sangha of monks. That merchant personally served various kinds of fine foods to the Sangha of monks headed by the Buddha. When the Buddha had finished his meal and had washed his hands and bowl, the merchant sat down to one side and said, “Sir, I’ve had these sixty dwellings built in order to make merit and for the purpose of going to heaven. What should I do now?”

original: “Tena hi tvaṁ, gahapati, te saṭṭhivihāre āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa patiṭṭhāpehī”ti.
text: “Well then, give those sixty dwellings to the Sangha as a whole, both present and future.”

original: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho rājagahako seṭṭhī bhagavato paṭissutvā te saṭṭhivihāre āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa patiṭṭhāpesi.
text: Saying, “Yes, sir,” he did just that.

original: Atha kho bhagavā rājagahakaṁ seṭṭhiṁ imāhi gāthāhi anumodi—
text: The Buddha then expressed his appreciation to the merchant with these verses:

original:
“Sītaṁ uṇhaṁ paṭihanti,
tato vāḷamigāni ca;
Sarīsape ca makase,
sisire cāpi vuṭṭhiyo.
text:
“Cold and heat are kept away,
And so are predatory beasts,
And creeping animals and mosquitoes,
And also chill and rain.

original:
Tato vātātapo ghoro,
sañjāto paṭihaññati;
Leṇatthañca sukhatthañca,
jhāyituñca vipassituṁ.
text:
They keep away the wind and burning sun,
When those awful things arise.
Their purpose is to shelter and for happiness,
To attain absorption and to see clearly.

original:
Vihāradānaṁ saṅghassa,
Aggaṁ buddhena vaṇṇitaṁ;
Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso,
Sampassaṁ atthamattano.
text:
Giving dwellings to the Sangha
Is praised as the best by the Buddha.
Therefore the wise man,
Seeing what’s beneficial for himself,

original:
Vihāre kāraye ramme,
vāsayettha bahussute;
Tesaṁ annañca pānañca,
vatthasenāsanāni ca.
text:
Should build delightful dwellings
And have the learned stay there.
Food, drink, robes, and dwellings—
With an inspired mind,

He should give to them,
The upright ones.
They will give him the Teaching
For removing all suffering;
And understanding this Teaching in this life,
He attains extinguishment, free of corruptions.”

original: Atha kho bhagavā rājagahakaṁ seṭṭhiṁ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
text: The Buddha then got up from his seat and left.

original: Assosuṁ kho manussā— “bhagavatā kira vihārā anuññātā”ti sakkaccaṁ vihāre kārāpenti. Te vihārā akavāṭakā honti; ahīpi vicchikāpi satapadiyopi pavisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Hearing that the Buddha had allowed dwellings, people had dwellings built with care. But because the dwellings did not have doors, snakes, scorpions, and centipedes came inside. They told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭan”ti.
text: “I allow doors.”

original: Bhittichiddaṁ karitvā valliyāpi rajjuyāpi kavāṭaṁ bandhanti. Undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjanti. Khayitabandhanāni kavāṭāni patanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: They made a hole in the wall and bound the doors with creepers and ropes. Rats and termites ate the creepers and ropes, and the doors fell off.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṁ udukkhalikaṁ uttarapāsakan”ti.
text: “I allow door frames, and lower and upper hinges.”

original: Kavāṭā na phusīyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The doors did not fit the door frames.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āviñchanacchiddaṁ āviñchanarajjun”ti.
text: “I allow a hole in the door and a rope for pulling.”

original: Kavāṭā na thakiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The doors did not stay closed.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aggaḷavaṭṭiṁ kapisīsakaṁ sūcikaṁ ghaṭikan”ti.
text: “I allow door jambs, bolt sockets, bolts, and latches.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū na sakkonti kavāṭaṁ apāpurituṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The monks were unable to open the doors.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tāḷacchiddaṁ. Tīṇi tāḷāni— lohatāḷaṁ, kaṭṭhatāḷaṁ, visāṇatāḷan”ti.
text: “I allow a keyhole and three kinds of keys: metal keys, wooden keys, and keys made of horn.”

original: Yehi te ugghāṭetvā pavisanti, vihārā aguttā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: They lifted the latches with the keys and entered, but the dwellings were unprotected.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yantakaṁ sūcikan”ti.
text: “I allow bolts.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena vihārā tiṇacchadanā honti; sītakāle sītā, uṇhakāle uṇhā. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the dwellings had roofs of straw. When the weather was cold, they were cold, and when the weather was hot, they were hot.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṁ kātun”ti.
text: “I allow you to firm up the structure and then to plaster it inside and outside.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena vihārā avātapānakā honti acakkhussā duggandhā. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the dwellings did not have windows. It was hard to see and the dwellings were smelly. They told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tīṇi vātapānāni— vedikāvātapānaṁ, jālavātapānaṁ, salākavātapānan”ti.
text: “I allow three kinds of windows: railing windows, lattice windows, and windows with bars.”

original: Vātapānantarikāya kāḷakāpi vagguliyopi pavisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Squirrels and bats entered the dwellings through the gaps in the windows.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vātapānacakkalikan”ti.
text: “I allow cloth covers.”

original: Cakkalikantarikāyapi kāḷakāpi vagguliyopi pavisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The squirrels and bats entered in the gaps around the cloth cover.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vātapānakavāṭakaṁ vātapānabhisikan”ti.
text: “I allow shutters.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chamāyaṁ sayanti. Gattānipi cīvarānipi paṁsukitāni honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks lay down on the ground. They got dirty, as did their robes.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇasanthārakan”ti.
text: “I allow a spread of grass.”

original: Tiṇasanthārako undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The grass was eaten by rats and termites.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, miḍḍhin”ti.
text: “I allow benches.”

original: Miḍḍhiyā gattāni dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The benches were painful to lie on.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bidalamañcakan”ti.
text: “I allow wicker beds.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko masārako mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards the Sangha was offered various kinds of beds with legs and frames from a charnel ground. They told the Buddha.
title: 2. The allowance for beds and benches (1.2. Mañcapīṭhādianujānana)

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, masārakaṁ mañcan”ti.
text: “I allow the various kinds of beds with legs and frames.”

original: Masārakaṁ pīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered various kinds of benches with legs and frames.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, masārakaṁ pīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow the various kinds of benches with legs and frames.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko bundikābaddho mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bundikābaddhaṁ mañcan”ti.
Bundikābaddhaṁ pīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bundikābaddhaṁ pīṭhan”ti.
Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko kuḷīrapādako mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a bed with crooked legs from a charnel ground.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kuḷīrapādakaṁ mañcan”ti.
text: “I allow beds with crooked legs.”

original: Kuḷīrapādakaṁ pīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a bench with crooked legs.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kuḷīrapādakaṁ pīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow benches with crooked legs.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa sosāniko āhaccapādako mañco uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a bed with detachable legs from a charnel ground.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āhaccapādakaṁ mañcan”ti.
text: “I allow beds with detachable legs.”

original: Āhaccapādakaṁ pīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a bench with detachable legs.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āhaccapādakaṁ pīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow benches with detachable legs.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa āsandiko uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a square bench.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āsandikan”ti.
text: “I allow square benches.”

original: Uccako āsandiko uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a tall square bench.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccakampi āsandikan”ti.
text: “I also allow tall square benches.”

original: Sattaṅgo uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a sofa.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattaṅgan”ti.
text: “I allow sofas.”

original: Uccako sattaṅgo uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a high sofa.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccakampi sattaṅgan”ti.
text: “I also allow high sofas.”

original: Bhaddapīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a cane bench.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhaddapīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow cane benches.”

original: Pīṭhikā uppannā hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a small bench bound with pieces of cloth.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pīṭhikan”ti.
text: “I allow small benches bound with pieces of cloth.”

original: Eḷakapādakaṁ pīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a bench with ram-like legs.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, eḷakapādakaṁ pīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow benches with ram-like legs.”

original: Āmalakavaṭṭikaṁ pīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a bench with many legs.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āmalakavaṭṭikaṁ pīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow benches with many legs.”

original: Phalakaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a plank as a bench.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, phalakan”ti.
text: “I allow plank benches.”

original: Kocchaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a stool.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kocchan”ti.
text: “I allow stools.”

original: Palālapīṭhaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a bench made of straw.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, palālapīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow benches made of straw.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ucce mañce sayanti. Manussā vihāracārikaṁ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six slept on high beds. When people walking about the dwellings saw this, they complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” They told the Buddha.

original: “Na, bhikkhave, ucce mañce sayitabbaṁ. Yo sayeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t sleep on high beds. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu nīce mañce sayanto ahinā daṭṭho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: Soon afterwards a monk was bitten by a snake while sleeping on a low bed.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mañcapaṭipādakan”ti.
text: “I allow bed supports.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ucce mañcapaṭipādake dhārenti, saha mañcapaṭipādakehi pavedhenti. Manussā vihāracārikaṁ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The monks from the group of six used high bed supports and then made the beds shake. When people walking about the dwellings saw this, they complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, uccā mañcapaṭipādakā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgulaparamaṁ mañcapaṭipādakan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use high bed supports. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow bed supports that are at the most eight standard fingerbreadths long.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa suttaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered string.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, suttaṁ mañcaṁ veṭhetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to wrap the beds with string.”

original: Aṅgāni bahusuttaṁ pariyādiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The limbs of the bed took up a lot of string.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṅge vijjhitvā aṭṭhapadakaṁ veṭhetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to perforate the limbs and wrap with a cross weaving.”

original: Coḷakaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a cloth.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cimilikaṁ kātun”ti.
text: “I allow you to make a mat underlay.”

original: Tūlikā uppannā hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered a cotton-down quilt.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vijaṭetvā bibbohanaṁ kātuṁ. Tīṇi tūlāni— rukkhatūlaṁ, latātūlaṁ, poṭakitūlan”ti.
text: “I allow you to remove the cotton down and make pillows. There are three kinds of cotton down: cotton down from trees, cotton down from creepers, and cotton down from grass.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū addhakāyikāni bibbohanāni dhārenti. Manussā vihāracārikaṁ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The monks from the group of six used pillows that were half the size of the body. When people walking about the dwellings saw this, they complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”

original: “Na, bhikkhave, aḍḍhakāyikāni bibbohanāni dhāretabbāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sīsappamāṇaṁ bibbohanaṁ kātun”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t use pillows that are half the size of the body. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow you to make pillows the size of the head.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe giraggasamajjo hoti. Manussā mahāmattānaṁ atthāya bhisiyo paṭiyādenti— uṇṇabhisiṁ, coḷabhisiṁ, vākabhisiṁ, tiṇabhisiṁ, paṇṇabhisiṁ. Te vītivatte samajje chaviṁ uppāṭetvā haranti. Addasāsuṁ kho bhikkhū samajjaṭṭhāne bahuṁ uṇṇampi coḷakampi vākampi tiṇampi paṇṇampi chaṭṭitaṁ. Disvāna bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion in Rājagaha there was a hilltop fair. People prepared mattresses for the government officials: mattresses stuffed with wool, cloth, bark, grass, or leaves. When the fair was over, they removed the covers and took them away. The monks saw a large quantity of wool, cloth, bark, grass, and leaves abandoned on the ground. They told the Buddha.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca bhisiyo— uṇṇabhisiṁ, coḷabhisiṁ, vākabhisiṁ, tiṇabhisiṁ, paṇṇabhisin”ti.
text: “I allow five kinds of mattresses: mattresses stuffed with wool, cloth, bark, grass, or leaves.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa senāsanaparikkhārikaṁ dussaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The Sangha was offered furniture cloth.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhisiṁ onandhitun”ti.
text: “I allow you to cover the mattresses.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū mañcabhisiṁ pīṭhe santharanti, pīṭhabhisiṁ mañce santharanti. Bhisiyo paribhijjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The monks laid a bed mattress on a bench and a bench mattress on a bed. The mattresses split open.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, onaddhamañcaṁ onaddhapīṭhan”ti.
text: “I allow upholstered beds and upholstered benches.”

original: Ullokaṁ akaritvā santharanti, heṭṭhato nipatanti …pe…
text: They laid out mattresses without an underlay. They sank down.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ullokaṁ karitvā santharitvā bhisiṁ onandhitun”ti.
text: “I allow you to arrange an underlay, then to lay down a mattress, and then to cover it.”

original: Chaviṁ uppāṭetvā haranti …pe…
text: The covers were removed and taken away.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, phositun”ti.
text: “I allow you to sprinkle them.”

original: Harantiyeva …pe…
text: They were still taken away.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattikamman”ti.
text: “I allow you to make multi-colored lines.”

original: Harantiyeva …pe…
text: They were still taken away.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, hatthabhattikamman”ti.
text: “I allow you to make multi-colored lines by hand.”

original: Harantiyeva …pe…
text: They were still taken away.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, hatthabhattin”ti.
text: “I allow multi-colored lines by hand.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena titthiyānaṁ seyyāyo setavaṇṇā honti, kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi, gerukaparikammakatā bhitti. Bahū manussā seyyāpekkhakā gacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monastics of other religions had white beds, black floors, and red ocher walls. Many people went to see their beds.
title: 3. The allowance for the color white, etc. (1.3. Setavaṇṇādianujānana)

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vihāre setavaṇṇaṁ kāḷavaṇṇaṁ gerukaparikamman”ti.
text: “I allow the colors white, black, and red ocher in the dwellings.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena pharusāya bhittiyā setavaṇṇo na nipatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The white color did not adhere to the rough walls.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, thusapiṇḍaṁ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā setavaṇṇaṁ nipātetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to apply balls of husk, smooth with a trowel, and then apply the white color.”

original: Setavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti …pe…
text: The white color still did not adhere.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṇhamattikaṁ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā setavaṇṇaṁ nipātetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to apply soft clay, smooth with a trowel, and then apply the white color.”

original: Setavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti …pe…
text: The white color still did not adhere.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ikkāsaṁ piṭṭhamaddan”ti.
text: “I allow sap and flour paste.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena pharusāya bhittiyā gerukā na nipatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The red ocher did not adhere to the rough walls.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, thusapiṇḍaṁ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā gerukaṁ nipātetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to apply balls of husk, smooth with a trowel, and then apply the red ocher.”

original: Gerukā anibandhanīyā hoti …pe…
text: The red ocher still did not adhere.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kuṇḍakamattikaṁ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā gerukaṁ nipātetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to apply clay mixed with bran, smooth with a trowel, and then apply the red ocher.”

original: Gerukā anibandhanīyā hoti …pe…
text: The red ocher still did not adhere.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāsapakuṭṭaṁ sitthatelakan”ti.
text: “I allow mustard powder and beeswax.”

original: Accussannaṁ hoti …pe…
text: It was too thick.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, coḷakena paccuddharitun”ti.
text: “I allow you to wipe it off with a cloth.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena pharusāya bhūmiyā kāḷavaṇṇo na nipatati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: The black color did not adhere to the rough floors.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, thusapiṇḍaṁ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā kāḷavaṇṇaṁ nipātetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to apply balls of husk, smooth with a trowel, and then apply the black color.”

original: Kāḷavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti …pe…
text: The black color still did not adhere.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gaṇḍumattikaṁ datvā pāṇikāya paṭibāhetvā kāḷavaṇṇaṁ nipātetun”ti.
text: “I allow you to apply excreted clay, smooth with a trowel, and then apply the black color.”

original: Kāḷavaṇṇo anibandhanīyo hoti …pe…
text: The black color still did not adhere.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ikkāsaṁ kasāvan”ti.
text: “I allow sap and bitter substances.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vihāre paṭibhānacittaṁ kārāpenti— itthirūpakaṁ purisarūpakaṁ. Manussā vihāracārikaṁ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti— “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks from the group of six had pictures of women and men drawn in a dwelling. When people walking about the dwellings saw this, they complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” They told the Buddha.
title: 4. The prohibition against pictures (1.4. Paṭibhānacittapaṭikkhepa)

original: “Na, bhikkhave, paṭibhānacittaṁ kārāpetabbaṁ— itthirūpakaṁ purisarūpakaṁ. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mālākammaṁ latākammaṁ makaradantakaṁ pañcapaṭikan”ti.
text: “You shouldn’t have pictures drawn of women and men. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. I allow you to make garland patterns, creeper patterns, shark-teeth patterns, and the fivefold pattern.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena vihārā nīcavatthukā honti, udakena otthariyyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the dwellings were built on a low base. They were flooded.
title: 5. The allowance for foundations of bricks, etc. (1.5. Iṭṭhakācayādianujānana)

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṁ kātun”ti.
text: “I allow you to raise the base.”

original: Cayo paripatati …pe…
text: The mound collapsed.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṁ tayo caye— iṭṭhakācayaṁ, silācayaṁ, dārucayan”ti.
text: “I allow you to construct three kinds of raised foundations: raised foundations of brick, stone, and wood.”

original: Ārohantā vihaññanti …pe…
text: It was difficult to get up to the dwelling.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne— iṭṭhakāsopānaṁ, silāsopānaṁ, dārusopānan”ti.
text: “I allow three kinds of stairs: stairs of brick, stone, and wood.”

original: Ārohantā paripatanti …pe…
text: People fell down while climbing the stairs.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāhan”ti.
text: “I allow rails.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena vihārā āḷakamandā honti. Bhikkhū hiriyanti nipajjituṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the dwellings were accessible to the public. The monks were embarrassed to lie down there.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tirokaraṇin”ti.
text: “I allow curtains.”

original: Tirokaraṇiṁ ukkhipitvā olokenti …pe…
text: People lifted them up and looked in.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aḍḍhakuṭṭakan”ti.
text: “I allow half walls.”

original: Aḍḍhakuṭṭakā uparito olokenti …pe…
text: People looked over the half walls.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo gabbhe— sivikāgabbhaṁ, nāḷikāgabbhaṁ, hammiyagabbhan”ti.
text: “I allow three kinds of rooms: rectangular rooms, long rooms, and upper rooms.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū khuddake vihāre majjhe gabbhaṁ karonti. Upacāro na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion the monks made a room in the middle of a small dwelling. There was no access around the room.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khuddake vihāre ekamantaṁ gabbhaṁ kātuṁ, mahallake majjhe”ti.
text: “In a small dwelling you should make the room on the side, but in a large dwelling in the middle.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena vihārassa kuṭṭapādo jīrati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the base of the wall of a certain dwelling was deteriorating.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kulaṅkapādakan”ti.
text: “I allow timber supports.”

original: Vihārassa kuṭṭo ovassati …pe…
text: It rained through the wall.

original: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parittāṇakiṭikaṁ uddasudhan”ti.
text: “I allow protection screens and plaster.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno tiṇacchadanā ahi khandhe patati. So bhīto vissaramakāsi. Bhikkhū upadhāvitvā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavocuṁ— “kissa tvaṁ, āvuso, vissaramakāsī”ti? Atha kho so bhikkhūnaṁ etamatthaṁ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: On one occasion a snake fell from the grass roof onto the shoulder of a certain monk. Terrified, he screamed. Other monks ran up to him and asked him why he was screaming. He told them.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vitānan”ti.
text: “I allow canopies.”

original: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū mañcapādepi pīṭhapādepi thavikāyo laggenti. Undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
text: At that time the monks hung their bags from the legs of the beds and benches. Rats and termites ate them.

original: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhittikhilaṁ nāgadantakan”ti.
text: “I allow wall pegs.”
